question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=4x(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+5y(t)-12 \\ {y}^{′}(t)={x}^{2}(t)-4x(t)+2y(t)+2\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of ODEs above. An equilibrium point of the system is $[2,\,1]^{T}.$ Which of the following is the system obtained by shifting this equilibrium to the origin?
question.worked_solution:
To shift the system's equilibrium from ${x}^{∗}$ to the origin, we define the deviation vector

$$
u=x-{x}^{∗},
$$

where $x=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]$ and $u=[\begin{aligned}u(t) \\ v(t)\end{aligned}].$

In our case, we have

$$
u=x-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,⇒\,x=u+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{x}^{′}={u}^{′}.
$$

In coordinate form, this can be written as follows:

$$
x(t)=u(t)+2,\,y(t)=v(t)+1,\,{x}^{′}(t)={u}^{′}(t),\,{v}^{′}(t)={y}^{′}(t).
$$

Let's now substitute these into the given system.

- Substituting into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =4x(t)-{y}^{2}(t)+5y(t)-12 \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =4(u(t)+2)-(v(t)+1)^{2}+5(v(t)+1)-12 \\  & =4u(t)+8-({v}^{2}(t)+2v(t)+1)+5v(t)+5-12 \\  & =4u(t)+8-{v}^{2}(t)-2v(t)-1+5v(t)+5-12 \\  & =4u(t)-{v}^{2}(t)+3v(t).\end{aligned}
$$

- Substituting into the second equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & ={x}^{2}(t)-4x(t)+2y(t)+2 \\ {v}^{′}(t) & =(u(t)+2)^{2}-4(u(t)+2)+2(v(t)+1)+2 \\  & =({u}^{2}(t)+4u(t)+4)-4u(t)-8+2v(t)+2+2 \\  & ={u}^{2}(t)+4u(t)+4-4u(t)-8+2v(t)+4 \\  & ={u}^{2}(t)+2v(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the shifted system is the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{u}^{′}(t)=4u(t)-{v}^{2}(t)+3v(t) \\ {v}^{′}(t)={u}^{2}(t)+2v(t)\end{aligned}
$$
